thread:
jonah: Need artifacts for vendor security review — they asked for SIEM ingestion examples, proof of admin activity logging, and retention export process. POC deadline Thu. Anyone who can drop files?

maria: I can pull samples. Do they want CEF, Splunk HEC JSON, or raw JSONL? :thinking_face:

alex: We have audit events in JSONL and can emit CEF for SIEMs. Quick summary: Hosted = Splunk HEC + S3 export, Dedicated = syslog(S-5425)/HEC, Private = customer-managed connectors. Can provide signed export manifests for chain-of-custody.

teri: Customer specifically listed: 1) SIEM ingest examples, 2) retention policy + retention proof, 3) admin activity logs (user add/role change/permission grants), 4) immutable export checklist and sample manifest.

maria: I'll bundle: - redacted admin JSONL sample, - Splunk HEC snippet, - export_manifest + sha256, - retention-policy.pdf. ETA: EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

drive-bot: drive-bot uploaded file: redwood-siem-evidence-1876543210.zip -> https://secure.example.com/d/redwood-siem-evidence-1876543210.zip

jonah: thanks. also customer asked if we can stream directly to their SIEM (syslog over TLS) and what auth methods we support.

alex: Yes. Supported options: Splunk HEC (token) for Hosted, syslog over TLS (RFC 5425) agent for Dedicated/Private, S3 presigned URLs for bulk export. Auth: HEC token, mTLS for agent, signed manifest + KMS-signed metadata for exports.

maria: Note on PII: we redact or pseudonymize fields by default in exports unless DPA scoping allows raw PII. We'll include the field mapping doc.

jonah: can we provide a sample Splunk query for "who changed role X between T1 and T2"? they want to run a quick forensics check.

alex: Sure — Splunk example:
```
index=redwood_audit event.action=role_change | where _time>="2026-03-01" AND _time<"2026-03-10" | stats latest(actor) by target_user target_role old_role new_role
```
Elasticsearch DSL (high level):
```
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "term": { "event.action": "role_change" } }, { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "2026-03-01", "lt": "2026-03-10" } } } ] } } }
```

teri: They also want tamper-proof export proof — chain-of-custody plus signed timestamps.

alex: We include a manifest.json with manifest_sha256 and signed_by key id. Example manifest entry: { "manifest_sha256": "3f8b...e2c1", "signed_by": "redwood-kms-01", "timestamp": "2026-03-15T18:02:00Z" } (we'll sign with KMS and include verification steps in README).

maria: I'll include the verification script and instructions (how to check SHA256 + signature). Also adding a short risk-matrix mapping to SIG controls.

jonah: two quick commercial notes: will we charge for generating long retention exports (>90d)? customer may request 12 months for POC.

alex: For Hosted we can do ad-hoc exports; large-scale long-term retention is a paid add-on (storage + extraction labor). Dedicated/Private customers typically configure retention themselves; we can run a one-time extract for free for SMB-sized data but enterprise-scale exports are quoted.

maria: Confirmed. I'll note pricing caveats in the README.

jonah: great — maria, please share the secure link to the zipped evidence with the customer's sec team and cc sales by EOD tomorrow. I'll follow up after they review.

maria: Will do. Upload + README + short summary email draft. cc @jonah when I share. :white_check_mark:

jonah: Thanks everyone — I'll update the deal notes and flag any blockers after customer review.
